description: The Projector Output window (FR-102), granted NOTHING — and the file exists so that emptiness is a statement someone wrote rather than an omission nobody noticed (SEC-01, ADR-0041). An empty permissions list is the entire content: no app-defined command, and not core:event:default either. PRD 6.3 puts this window's whole lifecycle in the Rust Display Service and PRD 6.5 has the slide-advance hot path broadcast TO it, so what it needs is to receive, not to call; on the day it must listen for events itself, core:event:default is added here by the item that needs it and by nothing else. Before SEC-01 this file could not have helped: "windows" scoping binds ACL-gated commands only, and app-defined commands were not ACL-gated at all, so the output window could invoke list_monitors — and every command added after it — with no trace in any manifest (ADR-0041). src-tauri/permissions/ now exists, so an app-defined command can reach this window OVER IPC only through a capability that names it, and none does. At least three things this file does not and cannot cover, named here so its emptiness is not read as a wider boundary than it is. The count is left open deliberately: closed enumerations have been wrong three times in this repository, and the missing item was always the one nobody had looked for. First, plugin:__TAURI_CHANNEL__|fetch is exempt from the ACL inside tauri's own condition (webview/mod.rs:1823-1826), so it is callable from here whatever this file says; the cost is zero while the application creates no Channel, and the first item that creates one owns it. Second, ADR-0042: output.html and index.html share an origin, so script running in this window can reach the Control Panel document through BroadcastChannel, localStorage or a MessageChannel without an invoke and without touching the ACL at all. Third, pending.navigation_handler is None for this window, so it can be navigated to any remote URL and CSP does not govern top-level navigation; the ACL has nothing to say about how the document in a window got there, and that one is SEC-02's. None of the three is exploitable today — the frontend's only invoke() is in src/main/App.vue and it relays nothing — but a Control Panel that ever acts on a same-origin message hands this window the reach this file was written to withhold. src-tauri/src/commands/mod.rs states both in full. Do not give any capability that grants an app-defined command a glob such as "windows": ["*"], and do not name "output" in one: scripts/check-command-inventory.js rejects both, because a glob is precisely how this window would get its reach back without anyone reading a diff that says so. NFR-13, NFR-14.
